$comment: Contract between this fixture and the analysis engine.
Phase 1 asserts `stack` only. Phases 2-3 assert `findings` as each rule
lands; `implemented: false` marks a rule that does not exist yet.
description: SQLAlchemy models drifted from the SQL migrations that actually built the database. The ORM layer is internally consistent and the migrations are valid SQL; they simply disagree with each other.

findings.title: ORM model field has no corresponding database column
findings.note: Breaks every SELECT against products, not just writes.

findings.title: Column type differs between model and database schema
findings.note: Silent precision loss on money, which is worse than a crash.

findings.title: Query references a column that exists in neither model nor schema
findings.actual: Raw SQL selects and orders by last_counted_at, which is undefined

findings.title: Model declares a relationship with no foreign key in the database
findings.actual: supplier_id INTEGER with no REFERENCES clause

findings.title: Foreign key column is not indexed
findings.expected: An index on the join column
findings.actual: No index; the supplier join is a sequential scan

must_not_report.reason: suppliers matches its migration exactly and must produce no schema findings.
These columns agree across model and migration.
low_stock and list_products only touch columns that exist.
